title: Abrasive Wheels
summary: A damaged or badly mounted abrasive wheel can break apart while spinning. This talk covers guards, work rests, flanges and the ring test. The flange-size and blotter details come from OSHA's general-industry standard 29 CFR 1910.215; the construction rule is 29 CFR 1926.303.
talking_points: Use abrasive wheels only on machines with safety guards. The guard must cover the spindle end, nut and flange projections and stay aligned with the wheel.
Right before mounting, inspect the wheel closely and ring test it. Tap it gently with a light nonmetallic tool. A cracked wheel sounds dead, not clear, and must not be used.
The wheel must be dry and free of sawdust for the ring test, or the sound will be dull.
Check that the spindle speed does not exceed the maximum operating speed marked on the wheel.
Mount wheels between flanges that are at least one-third the wheel diameter. Flanges must be clean, flat, in good balance, and free of rough surfaces or sharp edges.
Use blotters (compressible washers) between the flanges and the wheel where required. All contact surfaces must be flat and free of foreign matter.
On offhand grinders, use a work rest kept within one-eighth inch of the wheel. Clamp it securely after each adjustment, and never adjust it with the wheel in motion.
Always keep the wheel guarded, whatever type of flange is used.
site_hazards_to_check: Missing, loose or misaligned wheel guard
Cracked or chipped wheel, or one that sounds dead in the ring test
Wheel marked for a lower speed than the machine spindle
Work rest more than one-eighth inch from the wheel
Dirt or debris between the wheel, blotters and flanges
discussion_questions: How do you perform a ring test, and what does a bad wheel sound like?
Where do we find the maximum speed for a wheel, and how do we check it against the machine?
Why must a wheel stay guarded even when flanges are in good shape?

attribution.notice: Adapted from 29 CFR 1910.215, Abrasive wheel machinery. Reproduced with attribution for jobsite safety training; not an endorsement by OSHA.

flags: Content is quote-accurate to 29 CFR 1910.215(a)(1)-(a)(4), (c)(1)-(c)(7), (d)(1)-(d)(3): guard covers spindle, nut, flange, ring test with light nonmetallic tool, dry and sawdust-free, spindle speed vs marked speed, flanges at least 1/3 wheel diameter, blotters, 1/8-inch work rest clamped and not adjusted while running, always guarded.

FIX MADE: the source is general industry (1910.215) but the talk did not say so. 29 CFR 1926.303 (verified) is the construction equivalent and covers guards, ring testing before mounting, the 1/8-inch work rest and safety flanges, but not the 1/3-diameter and blotter details. Added a general-industry disclosure to the summary; both citations retained.
